title: Hardship Settlement Pricing: Length of the Qualifying Hardship Hold
content:
# Hardship Settlement — Hold-Length Reductions

The hold record kept under Ridgeline's Hardship and Protective Holds — its start date and, once it has ended, its ended date — bears on the price of a Hardship Settlement offer under its Settlement Agreements.

**Rule.** The length of the qualifying hardship hold is counted in calendar days from the hold's start date to its ended date, or to the offer date while the hold is still active; where that hold lasted 180 days or more, the Hardship Settlement long-hold reduction of 2.0 points applies; where it lasted at least 90 days but under 180 days, the Hardship Settlement mid-hold reduction of 1.0 point applies; a shorter hold carries no hold-length reduction.

## Measuring the hold

| Hold status on the record | Length counted from the start date to |
|---|---|
| ended | the ended date |
| still active | the offer date |

## Ladder

| Length of the qualifying hold | Reduction |
|---|---|
| 180 calendar days or more | long-hold reduction, 2.0 percentage points |
| 90 to 179 calendar days | mid-hold reduction, 1.0 percentage point |
| under 90 calendar days | none |

## Hypothetical cases

1. A hold started 200 days before the offer date and still active: 200 days, 2.0 points.
2. A hold that ran 120 days and has ended: 1.0 point.
3. A hold that ran exactly 90 days: 1.0 point; 89 days: none. Exactly 180 days: 2.0 points.
